question: Olefiant gas belongs to which of the following functional groups?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Olefiant gas** is another name for ethylene, which belongs to the **alkenes** functional group.
 
• Alkenes are hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C).
 
• Ethylene (C₂H₄) is a simple alkene and is widely used in the chemical industry and in the production of polymers such as polyethylene.
 
• The term "olefiant" comes from the Dutch word "olefiant" meaning "oil-forming," referring to the oil-like substances that ethylene forms when it reacts with chlorine.
 
• Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons, which makes them more reactive than alkanes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkanes** are saturated hydrocarbons with single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• **Halo alkanes** are alkanes in which one or more hydrogen atoms have been replaced by halogen atoms.
 
• **Ketones** are organic compounds characterized by a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms.
 
• **Alkynes** are hydrocarbons with at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (C≡C).
 
• Understanding the differences between these functional groups is essential in organic chemistry.
